pass_a_gloss: But what I say will be clear: there are some who are puffed up because they are sons of governors and because they are of the lineage of those from secular offices of great rank. Such people, puffed up over an involuntary and indifferent matter, do not even have a plausible likelihood that the thing being compared to them for being puffed up is reasonable. There are those who are puffed up because they have authority to kill people, and those who are puffed up because they have received what is called among them 'progress' of such a sort as to behead people. 'The glory' of such people 'is in their shame.' Others are puffed up over wealth, not the true but the low; and others are puffed up, so to speak, over having a fine house or many fields. None of these things is worth boasting about; one should not be puffed up over any of these things. The plausible thing about being puffed up, when someone is puffed up because they are wise, and is puffed up while being conscious of themselves, that they have not touched sexual things from ten years old or even from childhood; and again another is puffed up because they wore bonds around those concerning Christ. Plausibility is here presenting that someone reasonably is puffed up, yet not even on these things is it reasonable to be puffed up in relation to the true word. Thus it is not even reasonable to be puffed up on these things. Paul had the material for being puffed up himself through visions, through revelations, through wonders and signs, through the labors he endured for Christ, through the churches he established while striving, where Christ was not named, founding a church. All these things were material for him, if it must be said with plausibility regarding being puffed up, that he would reasonably appear to some to be puffed up. But since even being puffed up over such things is not without danger, the gracious Father, as he granted him visions and revelations, so he gave him in the measure of grace >a messenger of Satan, to strike him, so that he would not be overly puffed up. And concerning this, he thrice begged the Lord that the angel of Satan might depart from him, the one given to him so that he would not be puffed up. And the Lord answered him (for Paul was worthy of a reply from the Lord) and said to him: 'My grace is sufficient for you; for my power is made perfect in weakness.' Therefore, on nothing should one be puffed up, for it follows that to be puffed up leads to falling, according to 'before a breaking, the heart of a man is lifted up, and before glory it is humbled.' These things are for 'Hear and give ear, and do not be puffed up, because the Lord has spoken.'
